Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide a customer-facing workspace containing Overview, Help Center, Growth Hub, Campaign Scheduler, Sales & CRM Agents, Notification Center, Tickets & Feedback, Application Settings, and Activity & Audit navigation.
Unnamed: 3: All listed customer navigation destinations are available to an authenticated user; selecting an item opens the corresponding workspace view; the active destination is indicated accessibly.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall scope customer-facing workspace data and actions to the signed-in tenant and the authorized application context.
Unnamed: 3: A user cannot view or act on another tenant's or unauthorized application's data by changing UI parameters, URLs, identifiers, or API requests.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide an overview with entry points to Help Center, Growth Hub, Notifications, and Tickets & Feedback.
Unnamed: 3: Each overview entry point opens its corresponding section; displayed summaries are sourced from the current authorized tenant/application context.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide tenant-safe knowledge and onboarding content, including setup, roles, first-run guidance, payment/receipt troubleshooting, notification setup, and support contact guidance.
Unnamed: 3: Authorized users can browse help articles; search filters the available articles; content is scoped according to the configured tenant/content access policy.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow authorized users to upload, organize, and browse approved documents and video assets for growth activities.
Unnamed: 3: An authorized user can add and organize an asset; asset metadata and access permissions are retained; unauthorized tenants cannot access the asset.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide application-specific campaign and post planning with connected-channel settings.
Unnamed: 3: A campaign draft can reference an application, channel, content/asset, objective, and planned schedule; the campaign remains scoped to the selected application.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide an approval process for proposed external actions before publication or execution.
Unnamed: 3: External action remains blocked until an authorized human approves the exact action and content version; approval outcome and approver are recorded.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall display application-level growth KPIs, including engagement, leads, and conversion, when the relevant data sources are connected.
Unnamed: 3: Each KPI is attributable to an application and reporting period; unavailable or disconnected sources are identified rather than represented as valid live data.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow an authorized user to create a campaign draft with campaign name, application scope, channel, scheduled date/time, asset/draft reference, and objective.
Unnamed: 3: Required campaign name and application scope are validated; saved draft retains all entered fields; no external publication occurs during draft creation.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall support the campaign lifecycle Draft → Review Requested → Approved or Rejected.
Unnamed: 3: Only permitted transitions are accepted; each transition records actor, timestamp, outcome, and campaign/content version; rejected campaigns cannot be published.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall bind an approval to the exact content version and scheduled action being approved.
Unnamed: 3: Any edit after approval invalidates that approval and returns the action to a state requiring review; execution checks the approved version matches the current version.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall execute scheduled campaign actions asynchronously and expose queued, running, retrying, and failed outcomes to users.
Unnamed: 3: Scheduling and execution continue independently of the browser session; the UI can display persisted execution state and next action; no browser polling is required to initialize the scheduler.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall use idempotency keys for retried campaign delivery actions to prevent duplicate sends.
Unnamed: 3: Repeated delivery attempts with the same idempotency key produce at most one external side effect; attempts and final outcome are traceable.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide an application-scoped campaign queue showing campaign, channel, content version, owner, approval state, schedule and delivery state.
Unnamed: 3: Users see only campaigns within their authorized tenant/application scope; queue state reflects persisted scheduler state rather than illustrative/demo data.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall support provider-neutral orchestration for sales, marketing, and CRM agents.
Unnamed: 3: Agent provider integrations are abstracted behind a provider-neutral interface; changing an underlying provider does not require changing the customer-facing workflow contract.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow a Sales Agent to prepare lead research summaries, qualification suggestions, follow-up drafts, and next-best-action recommendations.
Unnamed: 3: Agent output is presented as a recommendation or draft; it does not autonomously send messages or perform consequential actions.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow a Marketing Agent to prepare campaign briefs, channel-specific content, asset reuse suggestions, and schedule recommendations.
Unnamed: 3: Generated content and recommendations are reviewable; publication requires explicit human approval.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow a CRM Agent to summarize account activity, suggest field updates, and prepare follow-up tasks against the native EPER CRM.
Unnamed: 3: CRM writes are not performed until a human approves the proposed write; approval is checked against current permissions and target scope at execution time.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide an agent run monitor showing run ID, requesting user, tenant/application scope, queued/running/completed/failed state, retries, and sanitized error details.
Unnamed: 3: Every run has a unique run ID; state changes and retry attempts are visible; secrets and sensitive provider payloads are redacted from displayed errors.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide an approval inbox for proposed agent actions, including approve and reject decisions.
Unnamed: 3: Only authorized approvers can decide; the decision is recorded; approval does not bypass authorization, scope validation, content-version validation, or idempotency checks.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow authorized configuration of notification settings for a selected application.
Unnamed: 3: Configuration is associated with the selected application and tenant; changes are validated and auditable; customer UI never accepts raw private keys or service-account JSON.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall support shared tenant Firebase project, dedicated per-application project, and mixed project assignment topologies.
Unnamed: 3: Each application resolves to the configured topology; dedicated and shared configurations are isolated according to tenant/application policy; topology changes are audited.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall store and use secure references to notification provider credentials instead of exposing credentials in customer-facing forms.
Unnamed: 3: Only secret references are stored in application configuration; secret values are retrieved from an approved secret-management facility at runtime; secret values are never returned to the UI or logs.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow application administrators to subscribe to selected workflow status, payment/receipt, support ticket, and KPI threshold events.
Unnamed: 3: Only selected event types are delivered for the configured application; subscriptions can be changed; each subscription change is auditable.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow notification audiences to be configured as authorized application users, application administrators, or configured roles/groups.
Unnamed: 3: Recipients are resolved from current server-side authorization and application membership; users outside the configured audience receive no notification.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall expose recent notification delivery activity, including attempt IDs, timestamps, redacted error classes, and correlation IDs.
Unnamed: 3: Each delivery attempt can be traced from event through provider response; retry outcomes are visible; sensitive provider details are redacted.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow a customer to submit a defect, feedback item, feature request, or question for a selected application.
Unnamed: 3: Required type, application, title, description, and business impact are validated; an accepted submission receives a canonical ticket ID; evidence reference is optional.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow a customer to attach or reference supporting evidence for a ticket without exposing credentials or sensitive payment data.
Unnamed: 3: Evidence is access-controlled and associated with the ticket; secrets and prohibited sensitive data are not accepted or are appropriately blocked/redacted.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall support ticket review, triage, severity assignment, ownership, status progression, resolution, verification, and closure.
Unnamed: 3: Supported statuses include New, Triaged, Assigned, In Progress, Waiting for Customer, Resolved, Verified, and Closed; invalid transitions are rejected and recorded.
Unnamed: 4: Ticket workflow and admin status list

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow a customer to view and track tickets belonging to their tenant and authorized application.
Unnamed: 3: The customer can see ticket ID, status, assigned role/resource where permitted, priority, application, customer-visible thread, and next action; cross-tenant records are inaccessible.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide a threaded ticket conversation with customer-visible replies and support updates.
Unnamed: 3: Messages are ordered and attributed to their authors and timestamps; customer replies are appended to the correct ticket; internal staff notes are never exposed to customers.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide authorized Product Admin users with a cross-customer ticket queue and filters for type, severity, status, tenant, and application.
Unnamed: 3: Queue results are filtered server-side according to admin permissions; a customer role cannot access cross-customer queues by manipulating the UI or API.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall allow authorized support staff to assign tickets to resources and perform permitted status transitions.
Unnamed: 3: Assignment and status changes require server-side authorization; old/new values, actor, timestamp, reason, and correlation ID are retained in audit history.

Unnamed: 1: Internal notes and customer replies separation
Unnamed: 2: The system shall keep staff-only internal notes separate from customer-visible replies.
Unnamed: 3: Internal notes are accessible only to authorized staff; they are excluded from customer APIs, notifications, exports, and customer-facing views.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall support authorized export of ticket queue data with server-side scope enforcement and data redaction.
Unnamed: 3: Export is unavailable unless authorization, tenant scope, and redaction controls are enforced; exported records are auditable.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall count a ticket toward the P1 discovery threshold only when it has a canonical ticket ID, confirmed severity and impact, reproduction steps/evidence, duplicate disposition, triager, and confirmation timestamp.
Unnamed: 3: Unconfirmed reports, duplicates, and feature requests do not count; the confirmed count is derived from qualifying records and is auditable.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall change the P1 discovery gate to Review Required when 100 distinct, evidence-backed, triage-confirmed P1 defects are reached.
Unnamed: 3: Reaching 100 triggers a business review only; it does not automatically approve development, funding, prioritization, or release.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide application settings for application identity, application-specific configuration, roles, enabled modules, and integration provider references.
Unnamed: 3: Settings are tenant/application scoped; integration credentials are represented by secure references; changes are authorized and audited.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall resolve localized currency display and the actual amount charged from approved price-book rules rather than applying cosmetic currency formatting alone.
Unnamed: 3: The resolved currency and charge amount are derived from the applicable approved pricing rules; the amount submitted to the payment provider matches the resolved charge; the calculation is traceable.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall provide traceable activity for important configuration, ticket, and delivery actions.
Unnamed: 3: Each audit event records actor, tenant, application, timestamp, action, outcome, correlation/reference ID, and redacted change summary; audit data is access-controlled and tamper-resistant.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall enforce tenant scope and role-based authorization on every API, ticket, attachment, export, and action; UI menu hiding shall not be treated as authorization.
Unnamed: 3: Direct API/object access attempts outside the caller's authorized tenant, application, role, or assignment are denied and logged; tests cover object-level and function-level authorization.

Unnamed: 2: The workspace shall support responsive layouts, keyboard-visible focus, accessible navigation state, and usable form controls across desktop and mobile breakpoints.
Unnamed: 3: Navigation and forms remain operable at supported viewport sizes; focus indicators are visible; active navigation state is programmatically exposed; controls have usable target sizes.

Unnamed: 2: The admin workspace shall surface open ticket count, untriaged feedback, confirmed P1 count/target, and tickets at SLA risk when connected to live operational data.
Unnamed: 3: Each KPI is calculated from authoritative ticket/SLA records; disconnected or unavailable values are explicitly shown as unavailable, not fabricated.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall require severity to be confirmed through triage; customer submission alone shall not automatically classify a ticket as P1.
Unnamed: 3: Severity changes require an authorized triager and evidence/reason; severity history is retained; P1 qualification follows the evidence criteria.

Unnamed: 2: The system shall distinguish live connected data from sample, illustrative, disconnected, or prototype data in all workspace views.
Unnamed: 3: A value or action marked demo/sample/prototype is never represented as persisted or live; unavailable integrations and disabled actions are clearly identified to the user.
